# Disagreement Log — MMT Section 2 (4QMMT Section A continued + beginning of B)

## Summary
- **Total disagreements:** 12
- **Section:** A (continued) and opening of B
- **Nature:** Festival terminology, counting formulas, and the transition to halakhic rhetoric

---

### Disagreement 1 — Line 2:1: "Festival of Weeks" vs. "Harvest Festival"
- **EMET:** "Festival of-Weeks" (hyphenated literal of Chag ha-Shavu'ot)
- **LOGOS:** "Festival of Weeks" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "Harvest Festival" (dynamic, emphasizing agricultural context)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Festival of Weeks" — the name derives from the counting of weeks (shavu'ot), which is the very subject of this passage. PNEUMA's rendering obscures this etymological connection.

### Disagreement 2 — Line 2:2: "sabbaths" vs. "weeks" in counting formula
- **EMET:** "seven complete sabbaths" (literal of sheva shabbatot temimot)
- **LOGOS:** "seven complete Sabbaths" (formal, capitalized)
- **PNEUMA:** "seven full weeks" (dynamic)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "seven complete Sabbaths" — the Hebrew explicitly says shabbatot (Sabbaths), not shavu'ot (weeks). This distinction is theologically significant for the sectarian calendar.

### Disagreement 3 — Line 2:2: "sheaf of the wave offering" vs. "sheaf as a presentation offering"
- **EMET:** "sheaf of-the-wave-offering" (literal of 'omer ha-tenufah)
- **LOGOS:** "sheaf of the wave offering" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "sheaf as a presentation offering" (dynamic)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "sheaf of the wave offering" — "wave offering" is the standard English rendering of tenufah and is widely recognized.

### Disagreement 4 — Line 2:5: Festival of New Wine dating
- **EMET:** "on the third of-the-[fifth]-month" (literal)
- **LOGOS:** "on the third of the [fifth] month" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "on the third of the [fifth] month" (identical to LOGOS)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** All three agree on the date. No divergence requiring adjudication.

### Disagreement 5 — Line 2:7: "dash" vs. "splash"
- **EMET:** "shall-dash the blood" (literal of zaraq)
- **LOGOS:** "shall dash the blood" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "shall splash the blood" (dynamic)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "shall dash the blood" — "dash" is the standard translation of zaraq in sacrificial contexts, following established biblical translation convention.

### Disagreement 6 — Line 2:8: "tithe" vs. "tenth part"
- **EMET:** "tithe of-the-wine" (literal of ma'aser)
- **LOGOS:** "tithe of the wine" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "tenth part of the wine" (explanatory)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "tithe of the wine" — "tithe" is universally understood and more concise than PNEUMA's expansion.

### Disagreement 7 — Line 2:13: "pleasing aroma" vs. "aroma that pleases"
- **EMET:** "a pleasing aroma to-the-LORD" (literal of re'ach nichoach)
- **LOGOS:** "a pleasing aroma to the LORD" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "an aroma that pleases the LORD" (dynamic restructuring)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "a pleasing aroma to the LORD" — the standard biblical phrase. PNEUMA's restructuring is unnecessary.

### Disagreement 8 — Line 2:15: "Day of the Wood Offering" vs. "Day for Bringing Wood"
- **EMET:** "Day of-Wood-Offering" (hyphenated literal)
- **LOGOS:** "Day of the Wood Offering" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "Day for Bringing Wood" (dynamic, action-focused)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "Day of the Wood Offering" — preserves the technical festival name. PNEUMA's rendering, while clear, loses the formal designation.

### Disagreement 9 — Line 2:20: "rulings" vs. "legal rulings"
- **EMET:** "some of-our-rulings" (literal)
- **LOGOS:** "some of our rulings" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "some of our legal rulings" (dynamic, adds qualifier)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "some of our rulings" — the context makes clear these are legal/halakhic rulings; the added qualifier is redundant.

### Disagreement 10 — Line 2:21: "works of the Torah" vs. "practices required by the Torah"
- **EMET:** "works of-the-Torah" (literal of ma'ase ha-torah)
- **LOGOS:** "works of the Torah" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "practices required by the Torah" (dynamic expansion)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "works of the Torah" — this phrase is the document's title and a key theological term (cf. Paul's erga nomou in Galatians). It must be preserved in its compact form.

### Disagreement 11 — Line 2:22: "saw" vs. "perceived" vs. "recognized"
- **EMET:** "we saw in-you" (literal of ra'inu)
- **LOGOS:** "we perceived in you" (formal, elevated register)
- **PNEUMA:** "we recognized in you" (dynamic)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "we saw in you" — the simplest rendering is also the most faithful. The Hebrew ra'ah means "to see."

### Disagreement 12 — Line 2:23: "straighten" vs. "direct aright" vs. "guide rightly"
- **EMET:** "that-He-straighten your counsel" (literal of yashar)
- **LOGOS:** "to direct your counsel aright" (formal)
- **PNEUMA:** "to guide your decisions rightly" (dynamic)
- **SOPHIA ruling:** "to direct your counsel aright" — balances EMET's overly literal "straighten" with PNEUMA's loose "guide your decisions." The Hebrew yashar connotes making straight/right.
